heads.text: THE HORDE HAS A DRUMMER NOW

caps.text: The enemy siege tower, which the artist confused with a very tall goblin. Both are bad.
A goblin on a war beast. The beast is drawn more sympathetically than the goblin.
Our lever room. Forty levers, one labelled 'BRIDGE?', one labelled 'DO NOT'.
Our archers in the tower, drawn mid-yawn, as observed.
The horde's drummer. The artist could not draw sound and has drawn a headache instead.
The kitchen staff barricading a door with a table. The table is doing most of the work.

reps.text: Scouts say the horde marched three seasons to get here and seems determined to make it worth the walk. Hospitality staff have been instructed to provide nothing.
The broker was mid-trade when the horde appeared and asked whether the goblins might be interested in some fine stone crafts. They are not interested in crafts.
{who} was sent to pull the drawbridge lever, pulled the lever for the upstairs cistern instead, and is now very unpopular with the archers, who are damp.
Civilian alerts have been raised. Dwarves who ignore them will be assumed to be brave, busy or deaf, in that order.
The goblins appear to have brought a war banner and a list of demands written on the back of a stolen tapestry. The demands are mostly 'everything.'
The hospital has stocked fresh thread, cloth and splints, and the chief medical dwarf has stretched, cracked his knuckles and said 'here we go.'

kickers.text: The Herald will publish as usual, from the basement.
Do not trade with the besiegers. They are not a caravan.
{first} reminds everyone that the bridge is not lever 12.
Our sympathies to anyone currently on the surface.

heads.text: IT CAME FROM THE THIRD CAVERN
BEAST HAS ONE EYE, MANY OPINIONS
WEBS IN THE CORRIDOR. BIG WEBS.

caps.text: The beast, according to three witnesses who did not agree on the number of heads.
A footprint left in the cavern mud. The artist fell into it while measuring.
The creature is made of crystal, or glass, or possibly ice. It was very shiny and very cross.
Artist's impression of the beast's breath. Please hold your own breath while viewing.
The cavern entrance, with a 'NO' sign the artist added after the fact.
The cavern farmer who first spotted it, still pointing. He has been pointing for a day.

reps.text: The creature is described as a huge blob of molten glass with gleaming wings and a dreadful habit of looking straight at you. Nobody expected the wings.
Scholars consulted the library and found the creature listed under 'Do Not.' The entry was short and written in an obvious hurry.
{who} met the beast at the cavern farm and backed away so slowly that the crops grew noticeably during the retreat.
The beast reportedly spits a substance that causes blisters, coughing and deep regret. The chief medical dwarf has requested more soap and a different job.
Military planners proposed a cage trap. The beast is larger than any cage. The planners proposed a larger cage. The carpenter proposed retirement.
The creature has been seen sniffing the walls, which experts say means curiosity, hunger or a strong opinion about our masonry. All three are bad.

kickers.text: The cavern is closed for the season, or for good.
{first} reports a sudden interest in surface living.
Please stop leaving snacks by the cavern hatch.
Taxonomists have filed it under 'absolutely not.'

heads.text: THE FORT GROWS QUIETER BY ONE

caps.text: The empty seat at dinner. The artist drew it with great care and a lot of grey.
The tomb, drawn before the bookkeeper assigned it, so it is labelled 'TOMB (TBD).'
A mug raised in salute. The artist drew forty mugs, because everyone raised one.
The deceased's favourite chair, already claimed by three different dwarves.
Artist's impression of eternal rest: a very long nap with no hauling in it.
A dwarf carrying a coffin alone. Nobody helped. That is hauling for you.

reps.text: {first} is survived by a bedroom full of crafted goods, a grudge against one particular door, and a well-worn stool nobody is permitted to sit on.
The tavern keeper has retired {first}'s regular stool for one week, after which it returns to service, because stools do not grow on trees, and we have no trees.
Friends recall that {first} once spent an entire season admiring a fine table. The table has been invited to the funeral and placed near the front.
A job has been posted to carry the body to the tombs. Three dwarves accepted it. One actually arrived. The other two are 'on their way.'
The mayor gave a short speech, mostly about himself, and closed by mispronouncing the deceased's name. Mourners agreed {first} would have expected nothing less.
The population of {fort} is now {pop}. The bookkeeper wrote it down, checked it twice, then left the office for a long, private cry in the stockpile.

kickers.text: Donations of ale to the wake are encouraged and inevitable.
{first} would have hated all this fuss.
The tombs are open; please queue politely.
A slab is on order. Do not let this become a ghost story.

heads.text: FORT SAYS GOODBYE TO A FRIEND
ONE LESS WAG IN THE HALLS

caps.text: The pet's collar, hung by the door. The artist drew it from memory and one small bell.
The pet's water bowl, untouched. The artist apologises for being this sad in ink.
The animal mid-yawn, a pose it held for most of its life.
The kennel, decorated with flowers the artist describes as 'mostly cave moss.'
A small parade of mourners. The parrot at the front is not real; the artist wanted a parrot.
The pet as drawn by the owner's child: four legs, a big smile and a crown.

reps.text: The animal will be remembered for following its owner everywhere, including into the forge, the barracks and, once, a private audience with the baron.
{who} has adopted a stony silence and asked that nobody say the word 'fetch' in the dining hall for a while.
Its favourite activities were sleeping, demanding food and walking directly under hauling dwarves. The fortress will be quieter, and slightly safer.
The animal trainer has written a heartfelt tribute that reads, in full: 'Good. Very good. The best.' It has been pinned to the kennel door.
A small engraving has been commissioned showing the pet on a sunny day. The engraver has never seen a sunny day and will be guessing.
With the loss, {fort} counts {pop} citizens and one sad, empty corner of the dining hall that nobody has the heart to walk through.

kickers.text: Belly rubs are suspended for one day in tribute.
{first} is accepting condolences and treats.
The kennel door has been left open, just in case.
Tributes may be left beside the bowl.

heads.text: STATUE TOPPLED IN FIT OF PIQUE
RAGE! ON THE STAIRS, OF ALL PLACES

caps.text: The toppled statue, which depicted a dwarf being calm. The irony was not lost on anyone.
The sheriff arriving, drawn as a beard with boots. He arrived at the very end.
A dent in the wall, roughly the shape of somebody's fist and somebody's opinion.
Artist's impression of the root cause: a bedroom the size of a cupboard.
A mug lodged in the ceiling. Nobody has asked for it back.
The calm-down room. It contains one chair, now in three pieces.

reps.text: The episode began when {first} was told the new bedroom would be ready 'soon,' a word with a long and bitter history in this fortress.
Witnesses say {who} toppled a statue, kicked a barrel and then sat down hard on the stairs, which cracked under the weight of the feelings involved.
The tavern has been closed for repairs and for a long community conversation about where furniture should and should not land.
Fortress justice has opened an investigation, which consists of the sheriff asking 'who did this' and everyone pointing at {first}.
Stress experts recommend fine meals, a nice bedroom and a long rest. The fortress can offer one of those, and it is not the meals or the bedroom.
After the outburst, {first} reportedly felt 'a bit better' and apologised to a door. The door has not yet accepted the apology.

kickers.text: Repairs will begin once everyone stops being upset.
{first} is 'taking some time.' Please give it to them.
Do not mention bedrooms in the tavern this week.
The statue has been stood back up, cautiously.

heads.text: ARTIST AT WORK; DO NOT DISTURB

caps.text: The dwarf sketching on the workshop wall. The artist tried to copy it and got a nosebleed.
A hauler bringing a log to the door. He was shooed away. It was the wrong log.
Artist's impression of what is being made: a blank square marked 'SECRET.'
Strange symbols chalked on the floor. The cleaners have been told to leave them be.
The workshop window glowing at midnight. There is no window. The artist insists.
The dwarf's dinner plate, untouched for days. This worries the cook more than anything.

reps.text: {who} rose from bed in the middle of the night, said 'leather, and something soft,' and walked straight into the leather works, mildly evicting the tanner.
The demands on the door now include 'something old,' 'something green' and a word the bookkeeper believes means 'gem.' Haulers are searching under everything.
The mood has gripped {first} so completely that a passing noble was ignored outright. Witnesses called it the bravest thing they have ever seen.
Scholars are divided on whether moods come from the gods, the stone or bad cheese. All agree it is best not to interrupt, whichever it is.
Haulers have brought cloth, wood, bone and a rock. The dwarf took the rock and sent everything else back with a polite growl.
Neighbours of the workshop report humming, then hammering, then a long silence, then laughter. The laughter was the worst part.

kickers.text: Results expected soon, or never, or with spikes.
{first} requests no visitors and one very specific gem.
Please keep the stockpiles stocked, for everyone's sanity.
The Herald will not knock either.

heads.text: ARTIFACT NAMED; NOBODY CAN SAY IT

caps.text: The artifact on a pedestal. The pedestal is not an artifact, but tried its very best.
The item's name, written out in full. It runs off the edge of the page.
The creator's hands, which shook for a day afterward. The artist's hands shook too.
The artifact, encircled with bands of gold, studded with gems and smudged by the artist.
A queue of admirers. The queue went around the dining hall twice.
The bookkeeper, appraising. The bookkeeper fainted shortly after this drawing.

reps.text: The new treasure has been given a name meaning, roughly, 'The Candle of Loud Agreement.' Its creator says the name came to them in a dream about stairs.
The object depicts the fortress itself, in which the fortress displays an image of the object. Philosophers have been asked to stop thinking about it.
{who} has been granted the title of legendary craftsdwarf, a new bedroom and the right never to haul again, which is the bit everyone is jealous of.
Neighbouring holds have already asked to borrow it for a festival. The answer is no. They will be informed in writing, also no.
The artifact is too valuable to use and too heavy to steal, which our security correspondent calls 'the best combination available.'
Rumours that the item is cursed have been firmly denied by its creator, who then quickly left the room for reasons they could not explain.

kickers.text: The artifact will not be lent, traded or used as a doorstop.
{first} is now insufferable, and has earned it.
Thieves are reminded that the guard is awake. Mostly.
Its full name will be printed in a later, larger edition.

caps.text: The masterwork under a cloth, at the creator's request, for dramatic reveals at dinner.
The workbench where it was made. The artist drew a halo over it. It is just a bench.
The creator's apprentice looking on, holding a much worse version of the same thing.
A dwarf admiring the piece so closely that their beard got into the drawing too.
The stockpile, with the masterwork placed on top of everything else, as demanded.
A close view of the joinery. The artist borrowed the jeweler's lens and had to give it back.

reps.text: {who} unveiled the piece at dinner, waited for applause, received some, and has been describing the applause in detail ever since.
The work is so fine that a passing noble demanded it for a mandate. The creator replied that it was 'already spoken for,' by the creator.
The apprentice asked how it was done. The master said 'practice.' The apprentice has asked to become a hauler instead.
Market watchers say the piece could fetch a fortune from the next caravan, assuming the creator can be separated from it, which seems increasingly unlikely.
{first} received a happy thought from the work, and the rest of {fort} received a long lecture on the importance of good tools.
Examiners agree the piece is 'masterfully designed' and have asked that this phrase stop being shouted down corridors at night.

kickers.text: The piece is not to be sat on, drunk from or traded.
{first} accepts compliments in person, daily, at length.
Rival workshops report a sudden rise in sulking.
The next masterpiece is already being bragged about.

heads.text: RICH VEIN; MINERS DO A JIG
THE ROCK WAS HIDING THIS ALL ALONG

caps.text: The magma sea, glowing. The artist used every orange on hand and borrowed a red.
A gem cluster drawn at five times scale, to match the miner's description.
Cross-section of the dig. The arrow labelled 'US' is extremely small.
The miner who found it, already asking for a better bedroom.
Artist's impression of the vein: a wiggly yellow line and the word 'MONEY.'
The first ore cart, drawn moments before it tipped over.

reps.text: Miners broke into a pocket of gems so large that the jeweler has requested a chair, a lamp and to be left alone for most of the season.
{who} reports striking a vein of ore 'thick as a beard and twice as shiny,' a phrase since written on the mine wall in charcoal.
Engineers confirm the heat rising from the lower tunnels is magma. They describe it as 'useful,' 'exciting' and 'please do not lean over.'
The forges are expected to be busy for years. The smiths have quietly asked whether they could be busy in slightly smaller amounts.
The new cavern is full of strange mushrooms, strange sounds and, according to one scout, a strange smell of wet dog. No dog has been found.
With the find, {fort} officially has something worth stealing. Our security correspondent has asked for a raise and a helmet.

kickers.text: Please do not lick the ore to test it.
{first} has been promoted to 'the one who found it.'
Digging resumes after a short celebration.
The jeweler is not taking visitors.

heads.text: NEW DWARVES; NEW NAMES TO FORGET
THE GATE OPENS, IN THEY POUR
NEW ARRIVALS SIZE UP THE TAVERN
REFUGEES OF A LESSER FORT ARRIVE

caps.text: The newcomers' names, written on a slate the artist ran out of room on.
A migrant carrying everything they own: one bag, mostly empty.
The housing officer looking at a list, then at the bedrooms, then at the list.
A small migrant child waving at a goat. The goat did not wave back.
New arrivals queuing at the dining hall. The queue is longer than the hall.
The migrants' old fort, as they describe it: 'smaller, sadder, damper.'

reps.text: The latest arrivals include a jeweler with no gems, a bone carver with no bones and a brewer with a very firm handshake. The brewer is already popular.
{who} arrived claiming to be a retired champion. The barracks have scheduled a sparring session to test this. The claimant has scheduled a long nap.
Newcomers were given a tour lasting four minutes, three of which were spent pointing at the tavern. All questions were about the tavern.
The population of {fort} has reached {pop}, and the bookkeeper has requested a bigger ledger and some quiet time alone with it.
One migrant asked where the farms were and was shown a single damp room of mushrooms. The migrant has since gone very quiet.
Housing officials have assigned the newcomers to 'the dormitory,' which is a corridor with a rug. The rug is said to be very nice.

kickers.text: Name tags are recommended for at least a season.
{first} has already joined a grudge.
The kitchen thanks you for your patience, and is crying.
Welcome. The rug is very nice.

heads.text: WAGON TOO WIDE FOR THE GATE

caps.text: The wagon, wedged in the entrance. The artist drew the haulers pushing. They were watching.
The liaison with a list of requests. The list goes off the page.
An exotic item for sale. The artist could not identify it and labelled it 'thing.'
The broker counting coins on her fingers. She ran out of fingers.
Pack animals resting in the depot. One is chewing the artist's sketchbook.
Traders laying out their goods. They have laid out a great deal of rope.

reps.text: The outpost liaison has arrived to discuss trade agreements, export quotas and 'concerns about your goblin situation.' The mayor has developed a sudden cold.
Traders offered rope, cages, cloth and one exotic bird priced like a small house. The bird has been insulting dwarves in at least two languages.
{who} was assigned to carry goods to the depot and has so far carried one stool, set it down and sat on it for the rest of the afternoon.
The wagon could not fit through the entrance, so the merchants have set up in the courtyard, where the weather can watch the haggling too.
The broker reports the merchants were impressed by our crafts and less impressed by our roads, our gate, our smell and our general attitude.
With traders in {fort} this {season}, citizens are reminded that selling the furniture out from under a noble is frowned upon, however tempting.

kickers.text: Haggling lessons are offered at the depot, free.
{first} bought a cage. Nobody knows why.
Trade agreements are binding, mostly.
The bird will not be staying. Please.

heads.text: BABY WEIGHS LESS THAN AN AXE
FIRST CRY HEARD IN THE DEEP

caps.text: The baby's tiny boots, which the leatherworker made from scraps and pride.
Grandparents crowding the cradle. The cradle is a barrel, cut in half.
The baby asleep. The artist tiptoed, which made no difference to the drawing.
Artist's impression of the baby's future: a small figure holding a very big hammer.
The whole tavern raising a mug. The baby raising a fist.
The baby's footprint, pressed into a clay tablet for the archive.

reps.text: The baby was born in the middle of a busy workday and immediately interrupted it, which elders say is the mark of a true dwarf.
{who} welcomed a child this {season}, and the tavern has started a betting pool on the first word. 'Ale' is the clear favourite.
The leatherworker made tiny boots, the carpenter a tiny cradle and the weaponsmith a tiny axe, which has been confiscated.
With the new arrival, {fort} counts {pop} citizens. The bookkeeper wrote the number in large, proud letters, then in smaller, careful ones.
Doctors report the baby is strong, alert and has already bitten one doctor. The doctor took it as a compliment and had it bandaged anyway.
The parents are said to be tired, happy and unsure where the baby should sleep. The fortress has suggested 'a drawer.'

kickers.text: The betting pool on the first word remains open.
{first} is asking for quiet. The baby disagrees.
Weapons are not appropriate baby gifts, again.
Lullabies may be sung in the tavern, softly.

heads.text: "I DO," SAYS DWARF. SO DO THEY.

caps.text: The vows being spoken. The artist wrote them down, but the ink ran.
The wedding toast: forty mugs and one wobbly speech.
A beard braided with silver wire for the occasion. The artist practised on his own.
The best friend, who lost the rings and found them in the stew.
The newlyweds dancing. Their feet are drawn as small blurs, out of kindness.
The couple's combined grudge list, nailed to their bedroom door.

reps.text: The pair have combined their belongings, their bedrooms and their grudge lists, which now share four goblins, one elf and a particular door in the east wing.
{who} married at the tavern while a performer played a slightly wrong tune on a bone flute. Guests agreed it set the mood, whatever the mood was.
The couple was introduced by a mutual friend, who now insists on being thanked at every meal, and is.
During the toast, the best friend called the couple 'two solid stones in one wall,' which was meant warmly and received with confused applause.
The ceremony took place in {fort} this {season}. Guests enjoyed stew, a song and the rare sight of the mayor saying something nice.
The newlyweds have requested a shared workshop. The manager has requested that they not use it to argue about dinner.

kickers.text: Wedding gifts may be left at the tavern, labelled.
{first} has promised to share the good chair.
The bone flute player is booked through spring.
Divorce is not a dwarven concept. Grudges are.

heads.text: HALLWAY CHILL HAS A NAME NOW

caps.text: The ghost peering into the kitchen. It cannot eat. It looks anyway.
A floating mug, with no hands visible. The artist wishes to move rooms.
The mason racing to the workshop with a slab block. The ghost is right behind him.
The ghost's favourite haunting spot: the exact middle of the busiest corridor.
A dwarf reading the ghost its own obituary. It did not seem to help.
Artist's impression of a cold breeze. It is a wiggly line. It was very cold.

reps.text: The spirit of {first} has been seen drifting down the main corridor, sighing at the stockpiles and pointing at things that were never put away properly.
A haunting in the tombs has become a full nightly tour, in which the ghost appears, moans and gestures pointedly at the empty memorial wall.
Witnesses say {who} has returned in spirit and has been rattling doors, toppling chairs and generally making the barrels feel unwelcome.
The mason was told to drop everything and engrave a slab at once. He dropped everything, including a block on his foot, and is limping to the workshop.
The tavern keeper reports a regular who arrives nightly, orders nothing and stares at the ale. The regular is translucent. The keeper is considering a ban.
Residents of {fort} who meet the spirit are advised to stay calm, avoid eye contact and, if possible, compliment its former craftsmanship.

kickers.text: The memorial slab is in progress, honest.
{first} is welcome to rest any time now.
Please stop leaving ale out for the ghost.
Haunted rooms will be cleaned when brave volunteers appear.

caps.text: The site of the collapse, with a sign planted that reads 'MIND THE GAP.'
A haul team clearing boulders. They are hauling one boulder each, slowly.
The architect's original plan, which has no ceiling drawn on it at all.
A dwarf sitting on the rubble eating lunch, entirely unbothered.
Artist's impression of the noise: a jagged line that runs right off the page.
The former staircase, now an uneven slope. A minecart is already rolling down it.

reps.text: A channeling project went one channel too far, and the floor above politely joined the floor below. Engineers are calling it 'aggressive renovation.'
{who} was digging out a bedroom when the ceiling came down and now has a very roomy bedroom with excellent air flow and no ceiling.
The architect insists the plans were sound and points to the plans, which turn out to contain no ceiling, only a doodle of a mug.
Officials cordoned off the area with a rope, two barrels and a sign. Dwarves walked straight past all three to have a look.
The collapse created a lovely open space that the mayor has already claimed as a private dining room, pending the removal of rubble.
Haulers report the rubble is plentiful. Masons report the blocks will be lovely. Everyone else would like to stop hearing rumbling, please.

kickers.text: Please channel responsibly.
{first} has been asked to stop pointing upward nervously.
The new open space is not a dining room yet.
Our ceiling remains in place at time of printing.

caps.text: The new legend practising on a dummy that has visibly given up.
A crossbow bolt in the exact centre of the target. Another is in the artist's hat.
The soldier's helmet, polished until the artist could see himself in it.
The barracks cheering. Two soldiers are asleep, as is barracks custom.
The drill sergeant, crying, then pretending not to be.
Artist's impression of courage: a beard blowing heroically in no wind at all.

reps.text: {who} reached legendary skill through sheer stubbornness, sparring daily for two years and losing to the dummy twice. That was long ago. The dummy remembers.
The drill sergeant called the achievement 'adequate,' then excused himself, and was later found weeping into a shield.
Militia records note that {first} has slain zero goblins, nineteen dummies and one particularly bold rat. Goblins are on the waitlist.
The new champion has asked for a better weapon. The weaponsmith has asked for steel. The miner has asked for a quiet life.
Strategists say {fort} is now defended by at least one dwarf who knows which end of the axe goes forward. This is a significant upgrade.
The champion chose a heroic nickname and asked everyone to use it. The barracks has chosen a different nickname instead.

kickers.text: The dummy has been replaced, and the old one honoured.
{first} will accept challengers after breakfast.
Goblins: you have been warned, again.
Sparring sessions are open to spectators and medics.
